hints.content: The graph of function $h$ is the graph of function $f$ shifted $12$ units to the right and down $4$ units.

To shift the graph of $y=f(x)$ right $12$ units, we can replace $x$ with $x-12$ in the equation. 


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two congruent absolute value functions labeled f of x and f of x minus twelve quantity on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph labeled f of x has a vertex at (negative six, eleven) and has an interval of increase from negative ten to negative six and an interval of decrease from negative six to one half. The graph labeled f of x minus twelve quantity has a vertex at (six, eleven) and has an interval of increase from negative one half to six and an interval of decrease from six to ten.

hints.content:
To shift the graph of $y=f(x-12)$ down $4$ units, we can replace $f(x-12)$ with $f(x-12)-4$ in the equation. 

[[☃ image 1]]



Notice that this is the graph of function $h$, and so $h(x)=f(x-12)-4$.

options.alt: Three congruent absolute value functions labeled f of x, f of x minus twelve quantity, and f of x minus twelve quantity minus four on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph labeled f of x has a vertex at (negative six, eleven) and has an interval of increase from negative ten to negative six and an interval of decrease from negative six to one half. The graph labeled f of x minus twelve quantity has a vertex at (six, eleven) and has an interval of increase from negative one half to six and an interval of decrease from six to ten. The graph labeled f of x minus twelve quantity minus four has a vertex at (six, seven) and has an interval of increase from negative one to six and an interval of decrease from six to ten.
